newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli dollar bonds end up after shekel declines.
newsitem.headline: Israeli dollar bonds end up after shekel declines.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Tuesday following a further decline of the shekel against the dollar, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.19 pct to 109.03
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.24 pct to 108.94
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.03 pct to 109.44
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.5 pct to 111.24
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 107.59
Volume including Makams was a moderate 151 million shekels.

"Investors are rushing to buy inflation-linked bonds following the recent decline of the shekel," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank. "The rise of the U.S. currency will eventually lead to higher inflation and investors are protecting themselves by buying CPI-linked bonds."

After winning back some of its losses from the end of June, the shekel has fallen 1.85 percent on the dollar since last Wednesday. It has shed lost 4.3 percent since the government instituted changes in the exchange rate mechanism and the Bank of Israel slashed interest rates on June 18.
Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance said that CPI-linked long bonds should continue rising causing yields to fall below four percent.

"Yields on long bonds are already at 4.05 percent and it's only a question of time before it will fall below four percent," he said. "Insurance companies and mutual funds are continuing to raise money and this is creating increased demand."
The Discount trader said that when yields near four percent investors have been selling but he said that the phenomenon would not continue for more than a few more weeks.
"In the long run the positive trend is expected to continue and eventually yields will fall below four percent," he said.
Activity in unlinked bonds and Makams was mixed with a positive bias, he said.
"With yields of 13 percent and inflation expectations of only 8.5 percent these bonds are still attractive for investors who do not have to pay tax on them," he said.
Dollar-linked bonds rose sharply as the shekel representative rate was fixed at 3.5730 against the dollar, compared with 3.5690 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.57 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
